question: Which Hindi novel by Munshi Premchand depicts the life of Indian peasants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Godan**, written by **Munshi Premchand**, is one of the most celebrated Hindi novels that portrays the struggles of Indian peasants.
 
• The novel, published in **1936**, is regarded as a masterpiece in Hindi literature and showcases the socio-economic conditions of rural India during the pre-independence era.
 
• The central character, **Hori Mahato**, is a poor farmer who struggles with poverty, exploitation, and societal pressures, reflecting the plight of the Indian peasantry.
 
• The title **"Godan"** translates to "The Gift of a Cow," symbolizing the social and religious obligation of gifting a cow, which plays a central role in the story.
 
• The novel critically examines the **feudal system, caste hierarchy, and indebtedness** that dominated rural India, making it a significant commentary on the socio-political landscape of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Munshi Premchand:**

 
 
• Munshi Premchand, born as **Dhanpat Rai Srivastava** in **1880**, is widely regarded as one of the greatest writers in Hindi and Urdu literature.
 
• He is known for his realistic portrayal of the lives of common people, especially the oppressed and marginalized sections of society.
 
• Some of his other notable works include **Nirmala, Gaban, Rangbhoomi**, and **Karmabhoomi**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Kurukshetra:** A novel by Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar', focusing on the moral and philosophical aspects of the Mahabharata war.
 
• **Gunjan:** Not written by Premchand; it is unrelated to the theme of rural life.
 
• **Urvashi:** A famous poem by Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar' that deals with themes of love and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Godan:**
 
 
• **Godan** is considered a pivotal work in Hindi literature, often referred to as a reflection of pre-independence rural India.
 
• The novel highlights issues like **landlord oppression, social customs, indebtedness, and poverty**, making it a socio-political critique of its time.
 
• Its realistic depiction of rural life and characters has earned it a timeless appeal, and it has been translated into multiple languages worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The novel is often studied in academic curriculums for its **literary merit** and historical relevance.
 
• It sheds light on the **impact of colonial policies** on Indian agriculture and rural communities.
 
• Godan has been adapted into films, plays, and television series, further cementing its place as a cultural and literary icon.
